row: What does the term 2/10, n/30 mean?
Pay within 10 days for a 2% discount
Pay within 2 days for a 10% discount
Pay at day 30 for a 2% discount
Get a 10% discount if paid within 2 days
Without the discount, the full amount is due within 30 days.
It is a cost of bringing the goods in.
Under the perpetual system, what must also be recorded at each sale?
Cost of goods sold is recorded with every sale.
Which is excluded from the acid-test ratio?
Which of the following accounts is used under a perpetual inventory system but NOT under a periodic inventory system?
Perpetual records Cost of Goods Sold with every sale. Purchases, Purchase Returns and Freight-In are periodic-system accounts (perpetual uses Inventory).
Credit terms of 2/10, n/30 mean that:
A 2% discount is allowed if paid within 10 days; otherwise, the full amount is due in 30 days.
A 10% discount is allowed if paid within 2 days.
The invoice must be paid within 10 to 30 days.
A 2% penalty is charged after 10 days.
2/10, n/30 = 2% discount if paid within 10 days, otherwise the full amount is due in 30 days.
Under FOB Shipping Point, who pays the freight costs and when does title pass?
Buyer pays; title passes at shipping point.
Seller pays; title passes at destination.
Seller pays; title passes at shipping point.
Buyer pays; title passes at destination.
FOB shipping point: title passes when the goods leave the seller, so the buyer owns them in transit and pays the freight.
Net Sales minus Cost of Goods Sold
Cost of Goods Sold minus Operating Expenses
Gross profit = net sales − cost of goods sold.

A company sells merchandise for $10,000 on account with terms 1/10, n/30. The customer returns $2,000 of merchandise and pays the balance within the discount period. What is the amount of cash received?
Net sales on the invoice = 10,000 − 2,000 = 8,000. Discount 1% × 8,000 = 80, so cash = 8,000 − 80 = 7,920.
Which of the following is a contra-revenue account?
Sales Returns and Allowances is deducted from sales revenue, so it is contra-revenue. Purchase Discounts is a contra-purchases/inventory account.
In a perpetual inventory system, a return of defective merchandise by a purchaser is recorded by crediting:
Perpetual system: the buyer credits Inventory for returned goods (periodic would credit Purchase Returns and Allowances).
Freight-Out is classified on a multiple-step income statement as:
Freight-out is the seller's delivery cost, an operating (selling) expense, not part of COGS.
If Beginning Inventory is $40,000, Cost of Goods Purchased is $250,000, and Ending Inventory is $50,000, what is Cost of Goods Sold?
Which entry is required when a company sells goods on account under a perpetual system?
Debit Accounts Receivable, Credit Sales; AND Debit Cost of Goods Sold, Credit Inventory.
Debit Accounts Receivable, Credit Sales only.
Debit Inventory, Credit Cost of Goods Sold.
Perpetual: record the sale (Dr Accounts Receivable, Cr Sales) and the cost (Dr COGS, Cr Inventory) at the same time.
Net Sales equals Sales Revenue minus:
Sales Returns and Allowances and Sales Discounts
Net sales = sales revenue − sales returns and allowances − sales discounts.
The operating cycle of a merchandising company is ordinarily:
Longer than that of a service company.
Shorter than that of a service company.
A merchandiser must buy and sell goods, so its cycle (cash → inventory → receivables → cash) is longer than a service company's.
An income statement that shows several steps in determining net income is called a:
A multiple-step income statement shows gross profit and income from operations on the way to net income.
Gross Profit Rate is computed by dividing Gross Profit by:
Gross profit rate = gross profit ÷ net sales.
Under a periodic inventory system, Cost of Goods Sold is determined:
At the end of the accounting period.
Periodic: COGS is worked out at the end of the period from the physical count (BI + purchases − EI).
Which of the following is NOT included in Cost of Goods Purchased?
Freight-out is a selling expense. Cost of goods purchased includes purchases, freight-in, and is reduced by returns and discounts.
A physical count of inventory is necessary under a perpetual system to:
Check the accuracy of perpetual records and detect shrinkage.
Calculate Cost of Goods Sold for the first time.
A count checks the perpetual records and shows shrinkage (theft, damage, errors).
When a buyer pays freight costs under FOB Shipping Point in a perpetual system, the buyer debits:
Buyer pays freight under FOB shipping point; in a perpetual system it is part of inventory cost: Dr Inventory.
Income from Operations is calculated as:
Net Sales minus Cost of Goods Sold
Income from operations = gross profit − operating expenses.
Which account normally has a debit balance?
Sales Discounts is contra-revenue with a normal debit balance.
